questions.question: Padma awardee Arjun Singh Dhurve is related to which of the following folk dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baiga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padma Shri awardee Arjun Singh Dhurve is a renowned artist associated with the **Baiga folk dance**, a traditional dance form of the Baiga tribal community.
 
• The Baiga tribe is predominantly found in the central Indian states of **Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh**.
 
• Baiga dance is performed during important tribal festivals, celebrations, and rituals, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the Baiga community.
 
• Arjun Singh Dhurve has contributed significantly to preserving and promoting the Baiga dance on both national and international platforms.
 
• His efforts have brought widespread recognition to the Baiga tribal art form, ensuring its continuity for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baiga Tribe:**

 
 
• The Baiga are one of the prominent **Scheduled Tribes** in India, known for their distinct culture, traditions, and spiritual practices.
 
• They traditionally practice shifting cultivation, herbal medicine, and live in harmony with nature.
 
• Their art forms, including dance and painting, reflect their connection with the environment and spiritual beliefs.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Baiga Dance:**
 
 
• Baiga dance involves **rhythmic movements**, vibrant costumes, and the use of traditional musical instruments like the Mandar and Timki.
 
• The dance is often performed in groups, symbolizing unity and harmony within the community.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards:**
 
 
• The Padma Awards, instituted in 1954, are one of the highest civilian awards in India, recognizing exceptional contributions in various fields.
 
• They are divided into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, with Padma Shri being the fourth-highest civilian award.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Folk Art Preservation:**
 
 
• Preserving folk art forms like Baiga dance is crucial for maintaining India's **cultural diversity** and heritage.
 
• Recognizing artists like Arjun Singh Dhurve through awards ensures that traditional art forms receive the attention and respect they deserve.

questions.question: Which of the following awards is NOT conferred for excellence in dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lalit Kala Akademi Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lalit Kala Akademi Award** is conferred for excellence in the field of visual arts, including painting, sculpture, and other forms of fine arts, not dance.
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**, established in 1952, is given for exceptional work in the fields of music, dance, and drama.
 
• The **Kalidas Samman Award**, instituted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, honors outstanding achievements in classical music, classical dance, theatre, and visual arts.
 
• The **Padma Shree Award** is one of India’s highest civilian honors and is given for distinguished service in various fields, including arts, which encompasses dance.
 
• The **Lalit Kala Akademi Award** specifically focuses on visual arts and has no connection to dance, making it the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lalit Kala Akademi**

 
 
• Established in 1954, the Lalit Kala Akademi (National Academy of Art) promotes and propagates understanding of Indian art both within and outside the country.
 
• The Akademi organizes national and international exhibitions and awards scholarships and fellowships to support artists.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• India’s national academy for music, dance, and drama, it was set up in 1953.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards are considered the highest national recognition for performing artists, including dancers.
 
 
 
• **Kalidas Samman**
 
 
• Instituted in 1980, the Kalidas Samman is awarded annually by the Madhya Pradesh government.
 
• It is given in fields such as classical dance, classical music, theatre, and visual arts.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• The Padma Awards, namely Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shree, are among the highest civilian honors of India.
 
• They are awarded for exceptional and distinguished service in various domains, including arts, education, sports, and more.

questions.question: The 'Rath Yatra' festival of Puri is celebrated as the sacred journey of which of the following Hindu deities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Jagannath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Rath Yatra' of Puri is a grand annual festival dedicated to **Lord Jagannath**, one of the forms of Lord Vishnu.
 
• This festival takes place in the famous **Jagannath Temple** in Puri, Odisha, and is celebrated in the Hindu month of Ashadha (June/July).
 
• During the festival, the idols of Lord Jagannath, along with his siblings **Lord Balabhadra** and **Goddess Subhadra**, are placed on massive chariots and taken out in a grand procession.
 
• The chariots are pulled by thousands of devotees as an act of devotion, symbolizing the journey of these deities to their aunt's home at the Gundicha Temple.
 
• The Rath Yatra is one of the **largest religious festivals in the world** and attracts millions of devotees and tourists from across the globe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Jagannath** is considered a form of Lord Vishnu and is worshipped primarily in the state of Odisha.
 
• The Jagannath Temple in Puri is one of the **Char Dham pilgrimage sites**, which are considered highly sacred in Hinduism.
 
• The chariots used in Rath Yatra are massive wooden structures, rebuilt every year by a dedicated team of artisans following traditional methods.
 
• The festival represents the concept of equality as devotees from all castes and creeds participate in pulling the chariots.
 
• The Rath Yatra is also referred to as the **Festival of Chariots**, and similar celebrations are held in various parts of India and abroad, especially by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON).

questions.question: Which of the following are the amounts of nutrients in a keto diet?

options.text: Only taking high number of vitamins and minerals
High protein and fat, carbohydrates in a low amount
High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate
High carbohydrate, proper amount of protein and low fat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ketogenic diet is characterized by consuming **high amounts of fat**, adequate protein, and **low carbohydrate levels**.
 
• This macronutrient distribution typically includes **70-75% of calories from fat**, 20-25% from protein, and **5-10% from carbohydrates**.
 
• The goal of a keto diet is to induce a metabolic state called **ketosis**, where the body primarily burns fat for energy instead of carbohydrates.
 
• Low carbohydrate intake restricts glucose availability, leading to the production of **ketone bodies**, which serve as an alternative energy source.
 
• A keto diet is often used for therapeutic purposes, such as managing **epilepsy**, and has gained popularity for weight loss and improving metabolic health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ketosis:**

 
 
• Ketosis is a metabolic state where the body uses fat-derived ketone bodies instead of glucose as its primary energy source.
 
• It is achieved by limiting carbohydrate intake and increasing fat consumption.
 
• Ketosis can be monitored through testing blood, breath, or urine ketone levels.
 
 
 
• **Ketone Bodies:**
 
 
• Ketone bodies are molecules produced in the liver during fat metabolism.
 
• They include beta-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate, and acetone.
 
• These compounds provide energy to the brain and muscles when glucose levels are low.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Keto Diet:**
 
 
• May help with weight loss by reducing appetite and increasing fat-burning.
 
• Can improve insulin sensitivity and blood sugar control.
 
• Used as a therapeutic diet for epilepsy, particularly in children with drug-resistant seizures.
 
 
 
• **Potential Risks:**
 
 
• May lead to nutrient deficiencies if not well-planned.
 
• Can cause side effects like fatigue, headache, and digestive issues, often referred to as the "keto flu."
 
• Long-term adherence may impact kidney health or cholesterol levels.
 
 
 
• **Carbohydrate Restriction:**
 
 
• Carbohydrates are limited to approximately **20-50 grams per day** on a standard keto diet.
 
• This restriction forces the body to switch from glucose to ketones for energy.

questions.question: The element with atomic number 59 lies in which block of the Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The f-block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The element with atomic number 59 is **Praseodymium (Pr)**, which belongs to the Lanthanide series.
 
• Lanthanides are part of the **f-block** of the Periodic Table, as their electrons fill the 4f orbital.
 
• Praseodymium is the third element in the Lanthanide series, with the electron configuration **[Xe] 4f³ 6s².**
 
• The f-block elements are also known as **inner transition elements**, and they include both Lanthanides and Actinides.
 
• Praseodymium exhibits unique magnetic, optical, and electronic properties, making it essential in applications such as alloys and glass manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lanthanides:**

 
 
• Lanthanides consist of 15 elements from atomic number 57 (Lanthanum) to 71 (Lutetium).
 
• These elements are known for their high magnetic susceptibility and are often used in high-tech applications like lasers and superconductors.
 
 
 
• **f-block Elements:**
 
 
• f-block elements are characterized by the filling of f-orbitals, which can hold up to 14 electrons.
 
• They are divided into Lanthanides and Actinides, and their unique electronic configurations give rise to special properties.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Configuration:**
 
 
• The general electron configuration for Lanthanides is [Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s².
 
• Praseodymium, specifically, has the configuration [Xe] 4f³ 6s².
 
 
 
• **Applications of Praseodymium:**
 
 
• Praseodymium is used in the creation of strong alloys for aircraft engines.
 
• It is also utilized in manufacturing colored glass and ceramics, especially yellow-green glass.
 
• In addition, it plays a role in producing high-strength permanent magnets.

questions.question: Which book has been authored by Rabindra Bharali?

options.text: The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music** is authored by Rabindra Bharali and focuses on the traditional and lesser-known aspects of Hindustani music.
 
• The book explores the evolution and decline of various forms of Hindustani music, aiming to preserve its heritage.
 
• Rabindra Bharali is well-known for his contributions to the study and documentation of Indian classical music.
 
• The book highlights the importance of reviving lost art forms and preserving the cultural legacy of Hindustani music.
 
• It serves as a valuable resource for music enthusiasts, researchers, and scholars interested in the rich history of Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Music**

 
 
• Hindustani music is one of the two main styles of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It originated in North India and is characterized by its improvisational nature and use of ragas and talas.
 
• The genre includes vocal, instrumental, and dance forms, with significant influence from Persian and Mughal traditions.
 
 
 
• **Ragas and Talas**
 
 
• A **raga** is a melodic framework in Indian classical music, while a **tala** is a rhythmic cycle.
 
• Ragas are associated with specific times of the day or seasons and are meant to evoke particular emotions.
 
• Talas provide the rhythmic structure and can range from simple cycles like teen taal (16 beats) to complex ones.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Classical Music**
 
 
• Efforts to preserve classical music include documentation, digitization, and teaching through institutions like the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• Books like **The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music** play a significant role in spreading awareness about declining art forms.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music and Global Impact**
 
 
• Indian classical music has influenced global genres, including jazz, fusion, and contemporary music.
 
• Renowned artists like Ravi Shankar have popularized Indian classical music worldwide.

questions.question: Andal was one of the most famous women ________ saints.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alvar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Andal** was one of the twelve Alvars, who were Tamil poet-saints devoted to Lord Vishnu in the Bhakti tradition of South India.
 
• She is the only female among the Alvars and is highly revered for her devotional poetry and deep love for Lord Vishnu.
 
• Andal is best known for her two works, **Tiruppavai** and **Nachiyar Tirumozhi**, which are considered significant contributions to Tamil devotional literature.
 
• Her devotion to Lord Vishnu is celebrated during the **Margazhi month** (December-January), especially in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Andal's compositions reflect themes of longing, love, and surrender to the divine, embodying the essence of the Bhakti movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alvars:**

 
 
• The Alvars were a group of 12 Tamil poet-saints who lived between the 6th and 9th centuries CE and were devoted to Lord Vishnu.
 
• Their hymns, collectively known as the **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**, are considered sacred texts in the Vaishnavite tradition.
 
• The Alvars played a significant role in propagating the Bhakti movement in South India.
 
 
 
• **Tiruppavai:**
 
 
• It is a collection of 30 devotional hymns composed by Andal in praise of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The Tiruppavai is recited daily during the Margazhi month and holds a central place in Tamil Vaishnavite tradition.
 
 
 
• **Nachiyar Tirumozhi:**
 
 
• This is another literary work of Andal that expresses her deep love and yearning for union with Lord Vishnu.
 
• It comprises 143 verses and is part of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement:**
 
 
• The Bhakti movement emphasized devotion and surrender to a personal deity, cutting across social and caste barriers.
 
• The Alvars and Nayanars (devotees of Shiva) were among the earliest proponents of the Bhakti tradition in South India.

questions.question: The original non-metamorphic rock that undergoes profound physical or chemical changes leading to the formation of a metamorphic rock is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protolith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **protolith** refers to the original, pre-existing rock from which a metamorphic rock is formed due to intense heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.
 
• The protolith can be of **igneous, sedimentary, or even earlier metamorphic origin**, depending on the geological environment.
 
• Examples of protoliths include **shale** (which can metamorphose into slate or schist), **limestone** (which transforms into marble), and basalt (which can turn into amphibolite).
 
• The transformation process involves **recrystallization, deformation, and chemical reactions**, but the rock remains solid during metamorphism.
 
• The study of protoliths is essential for understanding the **geological history** and tectonic settings of an area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metamorphic Rocks:**

 
 
• These are rocks that have undergone transformation from their original form (protolith) due to extreme pressure, temperature, or chemical processes.
 
• Common examples include **gneiss, marble, schist, slate, and quartzite**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Metamorphism:**
 
 
• **Contact Metamorphism:** Occurs when rocks are heated by nearby magma or lava.
 
• **Regional Metamorphism:** Happens over large areas due to tectonic forces causing high pressure and temperature.
 
• **Hydrothermal Metamorphism:** Involves chemical alterations caused by hot, mineral-rich fluids.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Processes:**
 
 
• **Recrystallization:** Formation of new mineral grains that are more stable under metamorphic conditions.
 
• **Foliation:** Alignment of minerals creating a layered or banded appearance, common in rocks like schist.
 
 
 
• **Regolith vs. Protolith:**
 
 
• **Regolith:** Loose, unconsolidated material covering solid rock, commonly found on Earth's surface.
 
• **Protolith:** The solid, original rock that transforms into a metamorphic rock under specific conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian constitution?

options.text: To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities
To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, National Anthem
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution are enshrined in **Article 51A** under Part IV-A.
 
• They were added through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• The duties include respecting the Constitution, National Flag, National Anthem, and promoting harmony and brotherhood among citizens, among others.
 
• **Obeying parents and discharging family responsibilities** is a moral duty but not listed as a Fundamental Duty in the Constitution.
 
• Currently, there are **11 Fundamental Duties**, with the 11th duty being added by the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**, which mandates parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6-14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• They serve as a reminder to citizens about their responsibilities toward the nation.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning they are not enforceable by law.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in India was inspired by the **Constitution of the erstwhile USSR**.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Abiding by the Constitution and respecting national symbols.
 
• Promoting harmony and renouncing practices derogatory to women.
 
• Safeguarding public property and striving for excellence in individual and collective activities.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," it brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the Fundamental Duties and also introduced the concept of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment**
 
 
• Added the 11th Fundamental Duty, which emphasizes education for children aged 6-14 years.
 
• It also made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.

questions.question: Which bonding material was mainly used to join the stones or bricks of 'The Great Bath' of the Harappan Civilisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum Mortar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gypsum mortar** was primarily used to bond the bricks and stones of the Great Bath in the Harappan Civilisation.
 
• Gypsum is a mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate (**CaSO₄·2H₂O**), known for its strong adhesive properties.
 
• The use of gypsum mortar ensured that the structure was watertight and durable, critical for the Great Bath's functionality.
 
• The Great Bath, located in Mohenjo-Daro, is considered one of the oldest public water tanks in the world, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the Harappan people.
 
• The Harappan Civilisation's use of gypsum mortar highlights their expertise in architecture and urban planning during the Bronze Age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Great Bath:**

 
 
• It is a large rectangular tank located in Mohenjo-Daro, measuring approximately 12m x 7m and 2.4m deep.
 
• The structure had steps leading down on both ends and was surrounded by a series of rooms.
 
• The Great Bath is believed to have been used for religious or ceremonial bathing.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Civilisation:**
 
 
• The Harappan Civilisation, also known as the Indus Valley Civilisation, flourished between 2600 BCE and 1900 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by well-planned cities, advanced drainage systems, and impressive architectural structures.
 
 
 
• **Building Materials in Harappan Architecture:**
 
 
• In addition to gypsum mortar, Harappans used baked bricks, mud bricks, and wooden structures for construction.
 
• The baked bricks were uniform in size, indicating a high degree of standardization.
 
 
 
• **Gypsum in Ancient Construction:**
 
 
• Gypsum was widely used in ancient construction due to its availability, ease of use, and ability to create strong bonding.
 
• Its water-resistant properties made it ideal for structures like the Great Bath.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cropping season in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has three primary cropping seasons: **Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid**, based on the climatic conditions and agricultural cycles.
 
• **Kharif season** begins with the onset of monsoon and includes crops like rice, maize, and cotton.
 
• **Rabi season** starts after the monsoon, during the winter months, and includes crops like wheat, mustard, and peas.
 
• **Zaid season** is a short cropping period between Kharif and Rabi, focusing on crops like watermelon, cucumber, and fodder.
 
• **Fang** is not recognized as a cropping season in India and does not have any association with Indian agriculture or its seasonal cycles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops**

 
 
• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of monsoon (June-July) and harvested in September-October.
 
• These crops require a lot of water and warm weather for growth.
 
• Examples: Rice, maize, sugarcane, cotton, jowar, bajra.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Crops**
 
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in summer (April-May).
 
• They require cool weather for germination and warm weather during the harvesting period.
 
• Examples: Wheat, barley, mustard, gram, peas.
 
 
 
• **Zaid Crops**
 
 
• Zaid crops are grown between Kharif and Rabi seasons, in the summer months (March to June).
 
• They are typically quick-growing crops that do not depend heavily on monsoon rains.
 
• Examples: Watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon, fodder crops.
 
 
 
• **India's Agricultural Seasons**
 
 
• India’s agricultural calendar is influenced by the monsoon cycle, which plays a critical role in determining the cropping patterns.
 
• Farmers plan their sowing and harvesting cycles based on rainfall distribution, temperature, and soil moisture levels.
 
• Agriculture in India is predominantly monsoon-dependent, making Kharif season crucial for food production.

questions.question: In January 2023, who was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitish Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nitish Kumar was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time in January 2023.
 
• He has been serving as the Chief Minister of Bihar since 2005, with brief interruptions.
 
• Nitish Kumar is the leader of the Janata Dal (United) party and has formed alliances with various parties over the years to maintain his position.
 
• His tenure has been marked by efforts to improve infrastructure, education, and governance in Bihar.
 
• He is known for switching alliances between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) in his political career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Janata Dal (United) Party:**

 
 
• A regional political party primarily based in Bihar.
 
• Founded in 1999 by merging various factions of the Janata Dal.
 
• The party's ideology focuses on socialism, secularism, and promoting the welfare of the marginalized sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Political Career of Nitish Kumar:**
 
 
• Nitish Kumar has held various positions in the Indian government, including Union Minister for Railways and Agriculture.
 
• He is recognized for implementing reforms in the railways during his tenure as Union Minister.
 
• He became Chief Minister of Bihar for the first time in 2000 but resigned within seven days due to lack of majority.
 
 
 
• **Political Alliances in Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar's political landscape often involves coalition governments, with alliances shifting frequently.
 
• Nitish Kumar has historically aligned with both BJP and RJD based on political circumstances.
 
• His coalition with RJD in 2022 marked a significant shift from his earlier alliance with BJP.
 
 
 
• **Governance Initiatives:**
 
 
• Nitish Kumar's tenure as Chief Minister has focused on enhancing infrastructure, including road connectivity and electricity supply.
 
• He has launched programs to improve education, such as bicycle distribution for schoolgirls and scholarships.
 
• Efforts have also been made to curb corruption and increase transparency in governance.

questions.question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A with column-B?

 
 
 
 
 
 

 **Column- A (Name of Vitamin)**
 **Column B (Deficiency Diseases)**
 
 

 i. Vitamin A
 a. Scurvy
 
 

 ii. Vitamin D
 b. Beriberi
 
 

 iii. Vitamin B1
 c. Rickets
 
 

 iv. Vitamin C
 d. Night Blindness
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: **__**i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deficiency of Vitamin A causes **Night Blindness**, a condition characterized by difficulty in seeing in dim light.
 
• Deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) leads to **Beriberi**, which affects the nervous system and cardiovascular system.
 
• Deficiency of Vitamin C leads to **Scurvy**, a disease causing bleeding gums, weakness, and delayed wound healing.
 
• Deficiency of Vitamin D causes **Rickets**, a condition resulting in weakened and deformed bones in children.
 
• The correct matching is:
 
 
• Vitamin A → Night Blindness
 
• Vitamin B → Beriberi
 
• Vitamin C → Scurvy
 
• Vitamin D → Rickets
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamins:** Organic compounds essential for the proper functioning of the body. They must be obtained through diet as the body cannot synthesize them adequately.
 
• **Night Blindness:** A visual impairment caused by a deficiency of Vitamin A, affecting the ability to see in low light or darkness.
 
• **Beriberi:** A disease caused by Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency, leading to symptoms like weakness, nerve damage, and heart problems.
 
• **Scurvy:** A disease resulting from Vitamin C deficiency, characterized by symptoms such as bleeding gums, joint pain, and fatigue.
 
• **Rickets:** A condition caused by Vitamin D deficiency, resulting in soft and weak bones, commonly seen in children.

questions.question: Who is the chairman of the State Planning Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chief Minister** of a state serves as the chairman of the State Planning Board.
 
• The State Planning Board is an advisory body that provides input on the development plans of the state and ensures alignment with the state’s socio-economic objectives.
 
• It plays a key role in formulating the state's five-year and annual plans, while ensuring effective utilization of resources.
 
• The board consists of experts, officials, and non-official members, with the Chief Minister acting as its head.
 
• This institutional mechanism facilitates coordination between various departments and ensures that plans are consistent with the national development agenda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Planning Board:**

 
 
• It was established to decentralize planning and ensure state-specific needs are addressed effectively.
 
• The board works in tandem with the **NITI Aayog** at the central level to align state and national development goals.
 
• Its composition usually includes economists, social scientists, and government officials.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
 
• It acts as a policy think tank for the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice.
 
• The Prime Minister is the chairperson of NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• India adopted the concept of five-year plans after independence, inspired by the Soviet model.
 
• The plans focus on economic growth, poverty alleviation, and social justice.
 
• The 12th Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last such plan before the transition to NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and oversees the administration of state departments.
 
• As the chairman of the State Planning Board, the Chief Minister ensures that development policies cater to the welfare of the state’s population.
 
• He/She also acts as a link between the state and the central government for funding and policy implementation.

questions.question: Magnolia and Laurel trees are found in which type of forest in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Montane Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Montane forests** are characterized by their occurrence in high-altitude regions, typically above 1000 meters, in India.
 
• Magnolia and Laurel trees are typically found in montane forests due to their preference for **cooler climates and higher altitudes**.
 
• These forests are divided into **tropical montane forests** and **temperate montane forests** based on elevation and temperature.
 
• Montane forests support a unique biodiversity, including species like **Rhododendrons, Oaks, and Ferns**, in addition to Magnolia and Laurel trees.
 
• In India, montane forests are primarily found in the **Himalayan region and the Western Ghats**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Thorn Forests:**

 
 
• These forests are found in regions with low rainfall (less than 70 cm annually).
 
• Vegetation includes thorny bushes, cacti, acacias, and euphorbias.
 
• Common in areas like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Punjab and Haryana.
 
 
 
• **Mangrove Forests:**
 
 
• These forests are located in coastal regions, especially in estuaries and deltas.
 
• Notable examples include the **Sundarbans**, home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.
 
• Vegetation includes mangrove species like Rhizophora and Avicennia.
 
 
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests:**
 
 
• These forests shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water.
 
• Common tree species include sal, teak, and sandalwood.
 
• Found in regions with 75-200 cm of annual rainfall, such as the Deccan Plateau and Central India.
 
 
 
• **Montane Forests and Climate:**
 
 
• The vegetation changes with altitude, ranging from tropical to temperate and alpine types.
 
• These forests play a crucial role in maintaining the hydrological cycle and preventing soil erosion in mountainous regions.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.21 billion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Census of India 2011, the total population of India was recorded at **1.21 billion**.
 
• This figure represents an increase of approximately **181 million people** since the previous Census in 2001.
 
• India’s population in 2011 consisted of **623.7 million males** and **586.5 million females**, marking a sex ratio of **940 females per 1000 males**.
 
• The Census of India 2011 was conducted by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• India accounted for **17.5% of the world’s population** in 2011, making it the second-most populous country globally, after China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census Overview:**

 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years and is the largest administrative exercise in the country.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India since its inception in 1872.
 
 
 
• **Density of Population:**
 
 
• The population density of India in 2011 was **382 persons per square kilometer**, an increase from 325 in 2001.
 
• Bihar recorded the highest population density (1106 persons per square kilometer), while Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest (17 persons per square kilometer).
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate:**
 
 
• The literacy rate in India increased to **74.04% in 2011** from 64.83% in 2001.
 
• The male literacy rate was 82.14%, while the female literacy rate was 65.46%.
 
 
 
• **Urban and Rural Population:**
 
 
• In 2011, **31.16% of the population lived in urban areas**, while 68.84% resided in rural areas.
 
• The urban population grew by 31.8% from 2001 to 2011, reflecting increased urbanization.
 
 
 
• **Sex Ratio:**
 
 
• The national sex ratio improved from **933 females per 1000 males in 2001** to 940 in 2011.
 
• Kerala recorded the highest sex ratio (1084 females per 1000 males), while Haryana had the lowest (877 females per 1000 males).

questions.question: In 1927, where was the conference against colonial oppression and imperialism, in which Jawaharlal Nehru participated on behalf of Indian National Congress, held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brussels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Conference against Colonial Oppression and Imperialism** was held in Brussels, Belgium, in 1927.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru participated in the conference as a representative of the **Indian National Congress (INC)**.
 
• The event was organized by **anti-colonial activists and international socialist groups** to promote solidarity among colonized nations.
 
• The conference discussed strategies to combat **colonialism, imperialism, and racial oppression** globally.
 
• It served as a platform for Indian leaders to align with other anti-imperialist movements and advocate India's freedom struggle on an international level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru's International Engagements**

 
 
• Nehru's participation in global conferences was part of his effort to connect India's freedom struggle with international movements.
 
• He believed in fostering solidarity with other oppressed nations to challenge colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Colonialism and Imperialism**
 
 
• Colonialism refers to the control or governing influence of a nation over a dependent territory, often exploiting its resources.
 
• Imperialism is the policy of extending a country's influence through diplomacy or military force.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 1927 Brussels Conference**
 
 
• The conference highlighted the shared struggles of colonized nations and emphasized the importance of collective resistance.
 
• It encouraged the exchange of ideas among leaders from Asia, Africa, and Latin America.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC) and Global Movements**
 
 
• The INC actively sought to internationalize India's independence movement through participation in global forums.
 
• This was a strategic move to gain support and legitimacy from other nations and international organizations.

questions.question: Duare Ration Scheme, which has been deemed legally void by the high court, was launched by which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Duare Ration Scheme** was launched by the state government of **West Bengal** in 2021.
 
• The initiative aimed to deliver food grains and other ration materials directly to the doorstep of beneficiaries under the Public Distribution System (PDS).
 
• It was part of the state government’s efforts to improve the accessibility of essential goods for economically weaker sections.
 
• The scheme was declared legally void by the Calcutta High Court in 2022, citing that it overlapped with the central government’s National Food Security Act (NFSA).
 
• The ruling highlighted that states do not have the authority to modify or create parallel schemes that conflict with central legislation like the NFSA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013:**

 
 
• The NFSA provides subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India’s population.
 
• It is a central government initiative aimed at ensuring food security for economically weaker sections.
 
• The Act covers priority households and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) beneficiaries.
 
• Under the Act, eligible households receive 5 kg of food grains per person per month at highly subsidized rates.
 
 
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS):**
 
 
• PDS is a government-managed system that distributes essential commodities like rice, wheat, and sugar to eligible beneficiaries.
 
• It aims to ensure food security and mitigate hunger, especially for low-income families.
 
• PDS operates through a network of Fair Price Shops (FPS) across the country.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal's Welfare Initiatives:**
 
 
• West Bengal has implemented several welfare schemes, including 'Khadya Sathi,' which provides subsidized food grains to 90% of the state’s population.
 
• The state government has also focused on doorstep delivery schemes like 'Duare Sarkar' to improve service accessibility.
 
 
 
• **Legal Conflict in Duare Ration Scheme:**
 
 
• The High Court ruled that the scheme conflicted with the central NFSA and lacked legal authority under the federal structure.
 
• The ruling emphasized that food distribution policies fall under the central government’s purview in India.

questions.question: Which reform was initiated by Lord Ripon for the welfare of labourers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Factory Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Factory Act was introduced by **Lord Ripon in 1881** to improve the working conditions of laborers in British India.
 
• The Act primarily focused on **prohibiting the employment of children below 7 years of age** and regulating their working hours.
 
• It mandated that **children aged 7-12 years could not work for more than 9 hours a day**, ensuring their protection and welfare.
 
• This Act also enforced the requirement of **periodic health inspections in factories** to ensure laborers' safety.
 
• The Factory Act of 1881 is considered a significant step towards **industrial labor reform** during the British colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ripon's Contributions:**

 
 
• Lord Ripon served as the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884 and is known as the **"Father of Local Self-Government in India."**
 
• He introduced reforms such as the **Financial Decentralisation** and the **Ilbert Bill**, which aimed to grant limited self-rule to Indians.
 
• He also repealed the restrictive **Vernacular Press Act** to promote freedom of the press.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Factory Acts:**
 
 
• The Factory Act of 1891 further improved labor conditions by reducing working hours for women and children.
 
• Later, the Factory Act of 1948, introduced after independence, laid down comprehensive labor laws in India.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Revolution and Labor Reforms:**
 
 
• The Industrial Revolution brought significant changes to labor practices, necessitating reforms to address exploitation and unsafe working conditions.
 
• Factory Acts were introduced in many parts of the world to regulate working hours, child labor, and workplace safety.
 
 
 
• **Child Labor Regulations:**
 
 
• The Factory Act of 1881 was one of the first attempts in India to regulate child labor during the colonial period.
 
• Modern laws, such as the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**, aim to eradicate child labor in India completely.

questions.question: The Ashokan inscriptions of Afghanistan are written in Aramaic and ______ scripts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ashokan inscriptions in Afghanistan are distinct because they are written in **Aramaic and Greek scripts**, showcasing the cultural and linguistic diversity of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• The inscriptions demonstrate the influence of Hellenistic culture in the region due to Alexander the Great's conquests and subsequent Greco-Bactrian rule.
 
• These bilingual inscriptions served as a means to communicate Ashoka's edicts to the local population, many of whom were familiar with Greek and Aramaic.
 
• The Rock Edicts found in Kandahar, Afghanistan, are among the most significant examples of these inscriptions in Greek and Aramaic.
 
• The use of multiple scripts by Ashoka reflects his policy of religious tolerance and administrative inclusivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aramaic Script:**

 
 
• An ancient script that originated in the Near East and was widely used as a lingua franca in the Achaemenid Persian Empire.
 
• It was adopted in regions under Persian influence, including parts of Afghanistan during Ashoka's reign.
 
 
 
• **Greek Script:**
 
 
• A script associated with the Greek language, introduced to the region during the conquests of Alexander the Great.
 
• Its presence in Ashokan inscriptions highlights the cultural exchanges between India and the Hellenistic world.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• Established by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE, it became one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• Ashoka the Great, the third emperor, is renowned for his efforts to spread Buddhism and promote ethical governance.
 
 
 
• **Edicts of Ashoka:**
 
 
• A series of inscriptions on rocks and pillars that outline Ashoka's policies, ethical principles, and promotion of Dhamma.
 
• They are written in multiple languages and scripts, including Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, and Aramaic.

questions.question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest child sex ratio (in the age group of 0-6 years)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Census of India 2011, **Mizoram recorded the highest child sex ratio** (in the 0-6 age group) among all states in India.
 
• The child sex ratio in Mizoram was **971 females per 1,000 males**, significantly higher than the national average of 919.
 
• The state’s strong emphasis on gender equality and education, particularly among tribal communities, has contributed to this high ratio.
 
• Mizoram’s society, predominantly composed of tribal populations, traditionally exhibits **more progressive attitudes toward gender parity** compared to many other regions in India.
 
• The high child sex ratio reflects **lower instances of gender-based discrimination** and female infanticide in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• It is defined as the number of females per 1,000 males in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• The CSR is an important indicator of gender equality and social health in a society.
 
 
 
• **National Trend in CSR:**
 
 
• According to the Census 2011, the national average CSR stood at **919 females per 1,000 males**, showing a decline from 927 in 2001.
 
• States such as Haryana and Punjab recorded some of the lowest CSRs, reflecting gender-based disparities.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing CSR:**
 
 
• Social norms and cultural practices, including **preference for male children**.
 
• Access to education and awareness about gender equality.
 
• Government initiatives and enforcement of laws against gender-based discrimination and sex-selective abortions.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** scheme was launched in 2015 to address the declining CSR and promote the welfare of girls.
 
• Strict implementation of the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** to curb sex-selective abortions.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman to be inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diana Edulji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diana Edulji** became the first Indian woman to be inducted into the prestigious **ICC Hall of Fame**.
 
• She was a pioneering figure in Indian women's cricket and captained the Indian women's team during her career.
 
• Diana Edulji played for India from **1976 to 1993**, establishing herself as one of the most successful Indian cricketers of her time.
 
• She was widely known for her left-arm spin bowling and her immense contribution to popularizing women's cricket in India.
 
• Edulji has also been recognized with the **Padma Shri**, one of India's highest civilian honors, for her contribution to sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Hall of Fame**

 
 
• The ICC Hall of Fame was launched in **2009** by the International Cricket Council to recognize the greatest cricket players in history.
 
• It honors players who have made significant contributions to the game of cricket at the international level.
 
• Inductees are selected by a special committee of cricket experts and historians.
 
• It includes players from all cricket-playing nations, highlighting their achievements and legacy in the sport.
 
 
 
• **Diana Edulji's Career Stats**
 
 
• Edulji played **20 Test matches** for India, taking 63 wickets at an average of 25.77.
 
• In **34 ODIs**, she took 46 wickets and was instrumental in many of India's victories.
 
• She was also known for her leadership, captaining India in multiple international matches.
 
 
 
• **Women's Cricket Milestones**
 
 
• India's women's cricket team played their first Test match in **1976**, with Diana Edulji as a key player.
 
• The team has since grown significantly, making notable achievements such as reaching the **finals of the ICC Women's World Cup** in 2005 and 2017.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian ICC Hall of Fame Inductees**
 
 
• Other Indian cricketers in the ICC Hall of Fame include **Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Anil Kumble, Rahul Dravid, and Sachin Tendulkar**.
 
• These players have been recognized for their outstanding contributions to Indian and world cricket.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities from the Carnatic Music correctly represent the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music'?

options.text: Manambuchavadi Venkatasubbaiyar, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar
MS Subbalakshmi, DK Pattammal and ML Vasanthakumari
Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Trinity of Carnatic Music** refers to three legendary composers: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri, who lived during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
 
• These composers are celebrated for shaping the structure of modern Carnatic music and enriching it with their unique contributions and compositions.
 
• **Tyagaraja** was known for his devotional compositions dedicated to Lord Rama, written primarily in Telugu.
 
• **Muthuswami Dikshitar** composed in Sanskrit and is famous for his kritis, many of which praise Hindu deities and draw inspiration from Indian classical ragas.
 
• **Syama Sastri** was known for his contributions to the kriti format in Carnatic music, composing in Telugu and Sanskrit, and his devotion to Goddess Kamakshi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kriti**

 
 
• A kriti is a structured and highly refined form of Carnatic music composition that typically includes pallavi, anupallavi, and charanam sections.
 
• All three members of the Carnatic Trinity significantly contributed to the kriti repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Raga System**
 
 
• The Trinity's compositions are based on the raga system, a foundational element of Indian classical music, which involves melodic frameworks for improvisation and composition.
 
• They explored and expanded numerous ragas, setting a benchmark for future musicians.
 
 
 
• **Devotional Themes**
 
 
• Most compositions by the Trinity are deeply devotional, dedicated to Hindu gods and goddesses.
 
• They infused spirituality into the music, making it a medium for worship and emotional expression.
 
 
 
• **Musical Heritage**
 
 
• The Trinity's works continue to be performed and revered in Carnatic music concerts globally.
 
• Their compositions are considered timeless treasures and have influenced generations of musicians and composers.

questions.question: Revenue account includes items related to the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**current financial year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The revenue account includes all income and expenditure items **pertaining to the current financial year** only.
 
• Items in the revenue account typically represent **operational activities** such as sales, services, and day-to-day business expenses.
 
• This account excludes any transactions that belong to **previous or future financial years**.
 
• The revenue account forms a part of the **profit and loss statement (P&L)**, reflecting the current year's financial performance.
 
• It ensures compliance with the matching principle of accounting, where revenues and expenses are matched to the period they occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Account:**

 
 
• This account records **income and expenditure** related to the core operations of an entity in a specific financial year.
 
• It excludes capital expenditures or revenues, which are reflected in the **capital account or balance sheet.**
 
 
 
• **Financial Year:**
 
 
• The financial year is a 12-month period used by governments and businesses for **accounting and tax purposes**.
 
• In India, the financial year runs from **April 1 to March 31**.
 
 
 
• **Matching Principle:**
 
 
• An accounting principle that ensures revenues and related expenses are reported in the same accounting period.
 
• This principle is crucial for accurate representation of an organization’s **financial performance**.
 
 
 
• **Profit and Loss Statement (P&L):**
 
 
• A financial statement summarizing the revenues, costs, and expenses incurred during a specific period.
 
• It is used to assess a company’s **profitability and operational efficiency**.
